chunks: Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, created the believer from the clay of Paradise, and created the disbeliever from the clay of the Fire.

And he (AS) said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, intends goodness for a servant, He purifies his soul and his body, so he does not hear anything of good except that he recognizes it, and he does not hear anything of evil except that he rejects it.

He (the narrator) said: And I heard him (AS) saying: The clays are three (types) — the clay of the Prophets, and the believer is from that clay, except that the Prophets are from its purest part; they are the root and for them is their excellence, and the believers are the branches from a sticky clay. Likewise, God, Mighty and Majestic, will not separate between them and their Shia.

And he (AS) said: The clay of the Nasibi is from black fashioned mud; and as for the weak ones (in understanding), they are from dust. No believer turns away from his faith, nor does a Nasibi turn away from his enmity, and God's Will prevails regarding them.

key_terms.المستضعفون: the spiritually/religiously weak or undiscerning — those who lack the clarity to commit fully to either faith or enmity
key_terms.المشيئة: the divine Will or Volition — God's ultimate authority over the final spiritual state of all created beings
key_terms.الناصب: Nasibi — one who harbors active enmity toward the Ahlulbayt (household of the Prophet); a technical term in Shia theology
key_terms.صفوتها: the elite/purest portion — the Prophets are described as being from the most refined part of the believing clay
key_terms.طينة: primordial clay — the cosmic substance from which different categories of human beings were created, determining their fundamental spiritual orientation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the clay from which believers and disbelievers were created?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches a cosmological doctrine of human origins based on primordial clay: believers were fashioned from the clay of Paradise, disbelievers from the clay of the Fire, and Prophets from the purest portion of the believers' clay. This teaching, addressed to early Shia communities seeking to understand why some people are inclined toward good and others toward evil, presents a predestinarian framework while affirming divine will as the ultimate authority over all outcomes. The doctrine of three types of clay — prophetic, believing, and hostile — was a key element of early Shia theology regarding the nature of faith and enmity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Al Nazar Bin Shuayb, from Abdul Ghaffar Al Jaazy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Created the Believer from the clay of the Paradise, and Created the disbeliever from the clay of the Fire’.

And he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And when Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Intends goodness with a servant, Cleans his soul and his body, so he does not hear anything from the goodness except that he recognises it, and he does not hear anything from the evil except that he rejects it’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I heard himasws saying: ‘The clays are three (types) – the clay of the Prophetsasws, and the Believer is from that very clay except that the Prophetsas, theyas are from its elite. Theyas are the roots, and for themas is theiras merit, and the Momineen (plural of Momin) are the branches from the sticky clay, thus Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic will not Separate between themas and theiras Shia’.

And heasws said: ‘The clay of the Hostile One (Nasibi) is from [15:26] from black mud Fashioned into shape; and as for the weak ones (of understanding), so (they are) from dust. Neither does the Believer change over from his Emān (belief), nor does the Hostile One (Nasibi) change over from his hostility, and for Allahazwj, there is the Volition regarding them’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from al- Nadr ibn Shu’ayb from ‘Abd al-Ghaffar al-Jaziyy from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, created the believers from the clay of paradise. He created the unbelievers from the clay of fire.

He then said, ‘When Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, decides to grant good to one of His servants. He purifies his spirit and body. Whenever he hears any good thing he recognizes it. Whenever he hears any bad things he dislikes them.’

I (the narrator) then heard him saying, ‘The clays are of three kinds: (a) one is the clay of the prophets from which the believers are also created, except that the prophets are made of the superior kind of clay. The prophets are the roots and the believers are the branches and for this reason they are more excellent than the believers. The believers are created from a stickier kind of clay. Thus Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious will not keep them apart from their followers.’

The Imam than said, ‘The clay of those who insult (‘ A’immah ) are from a black clay that smells foul. The weak ones are made from soil. The believers do not change their faith nor do evil doers (those who insult ‘ A’immah , recipients of divine supreme covenant) do so and Allah has a definite goal behind it.’”
